text:
Mira (Product): Quick sync on keys UI — we keep hearing confusion about disabled rotate/revoke buttons. Need final copy + accessibility behavior. Figma: https://figma.redwood/keys-disabled-flow :mag:

Carlos (Design): Problem: users see the Rotate button but it's greyed out with a tiny tooltip on hover. Mobile and keyboard users never see the reason. We should show the control but make the explanation discoverable for keyboard/SR users.

Evan (Frontend): Implementation idea: render the disabled button but include a visible inline link "Why is this disabled?" that toggles an accessible region (aria-expanded) with the explanation. That keeps keyboard discoverability and avoids tooltips. Also add aria-describedby on the button pointing to the explainer node.

Priya (UX Writer): Copy suggestion for explainer (short): "Requires Key Admin role. Request access from your org admin." Alternate short variant for narrow UIs: "Admin role required." For the inline link label: "Why is this disabled?" or more proactive: "Request access" if we wire the request flow.

Sam (Accessibility): A11y checklist: 1) the explainer must be focusable and revealed via a button with aria-expanded/aria-controls. 2) aria-describedby on the disabled control should reference the explainer so screen readers read the reason when the button receives focus. 3) Avoid relying on hover-only tooltips. 4) Provide a keyboard-accessible 'Request access' flow which opens a dialog (focus trap) or links to the workspace request flow.

Carlos (Design): Visual nit: the explainer region should be low-contrast background but with 4px rounded corners and 8px padding. On mobile collapse into a stacked layout under the controls. Keep animation simple (height expand) to avoid motion sickness.

Evan (Frontend): Behavioral note: if we surface a direct "Request access" CTA, ensure it opens the existing permissions request modal rather than a new flow. The disabled state should also include an aria-label like "Rotate (requires Key Admin role)" so sr users get the gist without toggling explainer.

Priya (UX Writer): Microcopy for disabled ARIA label: "Rotate key (requires Key Admin role)". Tooltip alt: "You need the Key Admin role to rotate keys. Request access from an org admin." Keep all variants < 90 chars.

Mira (Product): What about revoke? Users sometimes panic when they see revoke, fear they'll break things. We discussed a two-step confirmation: first click Revoke -> reveal inline confirmation row with checkbox 'I understand revoking will stop access' + optional reason. Then confirm button. Is that accessible?

Sam (Accessibility): That's better than a modal that forces typing. Make checkbox programmatic and focus should move to the confirmation row when revealed. Announce the confirmation row via aria-live polite. Also ensure keyboard users can tab to the optional reason textarea and skip it if they want.

Carlos (Design): UX microflow: Revoke button opens inline row: text 'This will stop any systems using this key.', checkbox + optional reason, then Confirm (destructive) and Cancel. Use a red outline for confirm, but maintain contrast. For compact rows, stack vertically.

Evan (Frontend): Logging: we'll send the optional reason to audit service if present. For confirm button disabled until checkbox checked. For SR label on confirm: 'Confirm revoke (checkbox checked)'.

Priya (UX Writer): Confirmation copy options: Short: 'Revoke key'. Warning line: 'This will immediately stop access for anything using this key.' Confirm button: 'Revoke key now' (destructive). Cancel label: 'Keep key'. Checkbox label: 'I understand revoking this key will stop access.'

Mira (Product): Empty state for keys list: push a clearer helper: headline 'No API keys yet', helper: 'Create scoped keys to let services call Redwood. Keep scopes minimal.' Primary CTA: 'Create key' and a secondary inline link: 'Learn about key scopes' linking to docs. Avoid auto-opening modals.

Sam (Accessibility): For empty state ensure the CTA is first in tab order and has descriptive aria-label e.g., 'Create your first API key'. Illustrations should be decorative (aria-hidden).

ops-bot: Added design checklist item: https://figma.redwood/keys-disabled-checklist (explainer pattern, revoke inline confirm, a11y notes). :white_check_mark:

Mira (Product): Action items: @Carlos update Figma with inline explainer pattern + revoke row, @Priya finalize short/alt microcopy, @Evan wire aria-describedby + focus behavior, @Sam to sign off a11y on the PR. Target next Tues. Thanks! :rocket:
